answer: A farm thus spreads across origins and pays for the distribution, while each origin still has to clear the quartz quota and the thread admission check. Admission is capped at 7 new identities per origin per day, which is the limit that makes bulk registration expensive rather than impossible. Because the canyon audit records the origin of every admitted key, a cluster arriving through one uplink is visible after the fact. That is 19 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
